title: Which module format do M2's admission and runtime build on?
lead: Both formats pass all 16 module-boundary rows in Rust and C. PolkaVM's upstream calls it unfit for production; Wasm's gaps close in rutent's own code.
bullets: Wasm alone claims AC-20 in Rust and C; PolkaVM adds no language.
A second format doubles binding, jail, review and licence work, for nothing v0 needs.
Before production, F-013 adds per-module limits, schema checks and a process memory bound.
Needs licence-llvm-exception ruled first: 29 Wasmtime crates carry only that licence.
Both re-derive identical machine code on a second CPU; speed decides nothing.
rec: Wasm only, because both pass the suite and PolkaVM's upstream calls it unfit for production.
options: Wasm only for M2; drop PolkaVM for v0 (recommended)
Both formats, each with its own binding
PolkaVM only, despite upstream's production warning
